LESSON: READING 2.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 2.2: Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why is the title of a poem or a story important? 2. How do we predict events in a story or poem?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and imagination is advanced as the learner participates in activities such as predicting the story by use of

pictures and visualising the event in the story as well as drawing pictures and posters on the events in the story.

• Learning to Learn is achieved as the learner retells a narrative or recite a poem and create a video of the recording

of the story.

Values:
Patriotism is promoted as the learner shows love for their country when they sing songs or recite poems related to

national celebrations.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills Education: effective communication is enhanced as the learner learns to communicate clearly through

pictures or story-telling.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies reading skills in all other areas of learning as they all require reading for comprehension.
